CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules (workflow, r-package, ci, native-code, correctness, assurance) come from the r-skills plugin’s rules/, loaded at session start because of the marker above. Never copy them here. Where this file and a shared rule disagree, this file wins for this package. Cloud sessions do not load the plugin and run without them.

What this is

zupmxode simulates population PK/PD models, written in a subset of the rxode2 model language, over NONMEM-style event records, in parallel over subjects, with no C compiler on the machine. Models are parsed in R, compiled to the package’s own IR, and turned into native code (or run in MIR’s interpreter) through zumir. It is a simulation engine with a C API for estimators; it is not an estimator, not a new model language, and imports nothing but zumir (design D20).

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0047. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides. The whole package rests on D2 (MIR through zumir), which is provisional on zumir’s Stage 0 spike; §11.1 of the design says what changes if the spike fails.

Current state

Stage 0 (package identity and CI) done 2026-11-15; no engine functionality yet. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #1 for v0.1.0. Siblings that will depend on it: zupmxfit (RFC 0072, through zupmxode_subject_eval()) and zupmxio (RFC 0046, Suggests both ways). It links to zumir only (zuexact left with design D21); zumir is not on CRAN yet, so it comes through Remotes: until it is, and its release gates this package’s submission.

Commands

  • make -C tests/c check: the C core built and tested without R’s headers. Part of the default loop once a stage touches src/core/.
  • bash tools/ci/platform.sh <os>: every per-OS check, as CI runs it.
  • Rscript tools/make-corpus.R: regenerates the oracle fixtures (about 2 minutes; needs rxode2, mrgsolve and nlmixr2lib). Occasional: when the corpus or an oracle changes.
  • tools/run-benchmarks [engine]: the §10 rows, appended to .agents/benchmarks.csv; run alone on an idle machine.

Architecture

See .agents/design.md §4 for the whole. Built so far:

  • src/core/ir.[ch]: the IR format, its verifier, a reference evaluator (the tests’ oracle and the fuzz harness’s, never an execution tier) and the math table. No R headers.
  • src/core/sched.[ch]: the event scheduler, one subject’s records to a sorted timeline (design §6.2 has the rules); src/zpx_sched.c its .Call; R/events.R pmx_ode_events(), the table’s checks and sched_timeline(), the tests’ view of a timeline.
  • src/core/linear.[ch]: the closed forms, the state carried exactly between events through the eigenvalues, with a matrix exponential where they meet (D21); src/zpx_solve.c walks a subject’s timeline with it; R/solve.R is pmx_ode_solve().
  • src/core/dopri.[ch]: Dormand-Prince 5(4) with dense output; zpx_solve_general() in src/zpx_solve.c runs LSODA or it over the timeline, with dense output across runs of observations, steady state by repeated dosing, and a failure as NA from where it happened.
  • src/zpx_lower.c: IR to MIR, one module and one function per block, through zumir’s C API and emitter; zumir_import() registers the table’s functions the C library lacks.
  • src/zpx_model.c: the model’s external pointer and finalizer, and the .Call entries. Failures of the IR or of MIR come back as status lists; R/model.R raises the classed condition.
  • R/compile.R: the compiler, R’s parse to IR text for the assembler: statements, names, linCmt()’s expansion, the classifier, and one generator for every block (DCE by statement, folding through the math table, CSE by value, ivl hoisting; compile_model(opts =) switches each off for the tests). R/pmx_ode_model.R is the export.
  • R/ir.R: the IR assembler; R/model.R: tiers, lowering, regeneration after readRDS() (D18).
  • src/zupmxode.c: registration only.

Invariants that are easy to break

These are fixed by the design before any code exists; each names the section that decides it.

  • No Imports but zumir (§2, §12, D20). Another runtime dependency breaks the “stock R installation” promise the package exists for. zumir is there only because R_GetCCallable() needs its namespace loaded.
  • Nothing under src/core/ includes R’s headers (tests/c fails to build if it does). The IR verifier in src/core/ir.c is the only thing between a saved IR and lowered code: every new opcode or operand needs its range check there, its refusal test in test-ir-verify.R, and a seed in tests/fuzz/corpus/.
  • C code never calls error() and never touches an R object inside the parallel region or zupmxode_subject_eval(); it returns status codes and writes into caller-owned buffers (§4.4, §4.6, §8). Breaking it makes the engine unsafe for estimators calling it from threads.
  • Random draws happen only in R, with R’s RNG (D7). C is deterministic, so results are reproducible from set.seed() at any thread count.
  • MIR is reached only through zumir’s C API and never vendored here (D14); the IR is the package’s own and nothing outside the lowering depends on MIR (D13).
  • The two tiers must give identical doubles, and output must be bitwise identical across thread counts (§6.3, §9). A difference is a bug unless traced to a recorded contraction.

Testing

Conformance suite: the oracle fixtures in tests/testthat/fixtures/oracle/, written by tools/make-corpus.R (design §7 says how). Regenerate them, never edit them; a new disagreements.csv row needs its note in disagreements.md, or test-oracle-fixtures.R fails.

Helpers:

  • helper-tables.R: expect_table_equal() at the §6.3 tolerances, through dazdiff when installed; table_differences() is the local route, tested on its own.
  • helper-oracle.R: reads fixtures and solves with rxode2. The generator sources it, so tests and fixtures solve the same way.
  • helper-models.R: hand-built IR models, each with its answer written in R; available_tiers() lists the tiers this session runs.
  • helper-compile.R: run_blocks() runs a compiled model’s blocks as the solvers will; r_eval_model() evaluates the same statements in R, the compiler’s oracle.

fixtures/math-reference.csv is the math table’s oracle, from tools/make-math-reference.R (needs Rmpfr); tests/fuzz/corpus/ and tests/fuzz/corpus-scheduler/ the fuzz seeds, from tools/make-fuzz-corpus.R.

The suite runs shuffled, top-level code included: build test data inside test_that() or in a helper, never at file level. Runtime: about 20 s locally, most of it rxode2 compiling three models.

Continuous integration

Shared r-actions workflows, called from .github/workflows/: R-CMD-check.yaml (with the Windows R-devel row), native-checks.yaml (valgrind, LTO, rchk, analyzers, cran-special; sanitizers from Stage 2, r-actions#68), gctorture.yaml (wide step on pull requests, step 20 daily and on dispatch), coverage.yaml (native: true), assurance.yaml and platforms.yaml. pkgdown.yaml builds and deploys the site.

platforms.yaml runs tools/ci/platform.sh: today the C core built and tested without R (make -C tests/c), Ubuntu only until Stage 2 adds macOS and Windows. Dispatch step-20 gctorture on the branch (gh workflow run gctorture.yml --ref <branch>) before merging a change to PROTECTs, finalizers or external pointers. The roadmap’s full stages are 2, 6, 8 and the three closing ones.

Vendored native code

liblsoda (https://github.com/sdwfrost/liblsoda, MIT), pinned at 16e49b428482e2efb552b0b4816a8ff8221e7efe (upstream’s last commit, 2018), in src/vendor/liblsoda/. tools/vendor/liblsoda.sh makes the tree from that commit and is the only place it is changed; tools/vendor/verify (the vendor workflow) rebuilds it and compares byte for byte. The patches, all in that script (8 to 11 found by Stage 6’s full run):

  1. No console output: printf/fprintf(stderr, …) become LSODA_LOG, which does nothing (the messages are in ctx->error).
  2. Only the sources upstream’s Makefile builds (not printcf.c, nor the #error stub ewset.c).
  3. _strdup_printf() allocates the NUL’s byte and checks malloc().
  4. The BLAS routines’ K&R definitions become prototypes (C23).
  5. lsoda()’s ihit starts at 0, and softfailure()’s loop variable no longer shadows the i its message prints (an uninitialised read).
  6. (void) for empty parameter lists.
  7. solsy() returns 0 rather than abort() for the banded Jacobian liblsoda never builds (CRAN: no C that can end R).
  8. A stray comma in lsoda()’s message for a repeatedly failed error test made %g read a char * and %s a double: a crash on that path.
  9. ERROR(), hardfailure() and softfailure() are C99 variadic macros, not GNU’s , ## __VA_ARGS__ (a significant warning under clang 23).
  10. _strdup_printf() has printf’s format attribute, so the compiler checks every message, measures into a one-byte buffer, not NULL, and returns NULL for a NULL format.
  11. The BLAS routines are lsoda_daxpy … lsoda_idamax: under the plain names the linker bound them to the BLAS R links (OpenBLAS’s Fortran idamax_, by pointer), so an int was read as an address. Every symbol is hidden too ($(C_VISIBILITY)), but R_init_zupmxode.

To change the pin or a patch: edit the script or manifest.tsv, run sh tools/vendor/liblsoda.sh, regenerate tools/vendor/checksums.sha256 (cd src/vendor && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs shasum -a 256), and run sh tools/vendor/verify. One instance per thread: each solve makes its own context. make -C tests/c builds it standalone and checks two contexts in turn against each alone.
